data.narrative: Completed Module 4 Critical Review - chose pattern-based review with targeted line-by-line on high-risk sections. Identified 2 CRITICAL (IDOR on DELETE/PUT teams), 2 HIGH (no name validation, no unique constraint), 1 MEDIUM (generic errors). Fixed IDOR vulnerability with specific authorization check. Verified with admin/non-admin tests. Learned five predictable AI failure modes, pattern-based review efficiency, hybrid approach for high-risk sections.

dimension_scores.observation: Fix prompt specific: names file, endpoint, exact check, query, error response, what NOT to change. Avoids vague 'fix security issue' prompts that produce wrong fixes.
dimension_scores.evidence: Fix prompt: 'In routes/invitations.js, POST /teams/:teamId/invitations checks authentication but does not verify user is admin of target team. Add authorization check that queries team_members for user_id=req.user.id AND team_id=req.params.teamId AND role=admin. Return 403 if no match. Do not modify other behavior.'

dimension_scores.observation: Reviewed all generated files across five categories: security, edge cases, error handling, naming, tests. Found IDOR vulnerability on invitation endpoint - any authenticated user could invite to any team. Found missing validation, error handling issues. Pattern-based review caught systematic issues efficiently.
dimension_scores.evidence: code-review-findings.md: 'CRITICAL: IDOR on invitation endpoint - no team admin check. CRITICAL: SQL injection risk. HIGH: No validation on team name emptiness. HIGH: No unique constraint on team name.'

dimension_scores.observation: One review pass sufficient for this complexity. Fix prompt specific enough to produce correct implementation on first try. No prompt spiraling. Verified fix with two tests (admin succeeds, non-admin fails). Pattern-based review (10-15 min) + targeted line-by-line on auth sections.
dimension_scores.evidence: Verification tests: Admin user POST /teams/{id}/invitations returned 201 (expected), Non-admin user returned 403 (expected). Fix worked on first iteration.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose hybrid review method: pattern-based first pass to catch systematic issues, then targeted line-by-line on high-risk sections (auth, data mutation, permissions). This gives 90% thoroughness in 50% time. Recognized AI failure modes are predictable. IDOR vulnerability caught because auth endpoint identified as high-risk.
dimension_scores.evidence: Decision: 'Pattern-based with targeted line-by-line on high-risk sections. Pattern-based catches predictable AI failure modes efficiently. Targeted line-by-line on auth/permissions catches critical issues. Gives 90% thoroughness in 50% time.'

dimension_scores.observation: Critical IDOR vulnerability identified and fixed. Security hardening applied. Code reviewed across five categories. Fix verified with tests. Code is more secure than initial AI output. One pass sufficient for this feature complexity.
dimension_scores.evidence: code-review-findings.md: Prioritized fix list with CRITICAL issues fixed. Verification tests confirm authorization check works.

strengths: Pattern-based review with targeted line-by-line on high-risk sections
Specific fix prompts that produce correct implementation
data.recommendation: Module 4 complete. Ready for Module 5 - Iteration Patterns.

public_evidence.artifact: Code review findings and IDOR fix
public_evidence.student_action: Reviewed AI-generated Team Collaboration code across five categories (security, edge cases, error handling, naming, tests). Identified IDOR vulnerability on invitation endpoint. Wrote specific fix prompt adding authorization check to verify user is team admin. Verified fix with admin/non-admin tests.
public_evidence.technical_detail: IDOR on POST /teams/:teamId/invitations - added query to team_members table checking user_id=req.user.id AND team_id=req.params.teamId AND role=admin. Returns 403 if no match. Verified: admin user gets 201, non-admin gets 403.
public_evidence.ability: Critical code review - catching security vulnerabilities in AI-generated code
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates essential AI engineering skill - reviewing AI output for predictable failure modes. IDOR vulnerability could allow any authenticated user to invite to any team. Specific fix prompt and verification shows ability to harden AI-generated code for production use.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Reflection: 'Security vulnerabilities, missing edge cases, poor error handling, confusing naming, inadequate test coverage are predictable AI failure modes.'
Reflection: 'Pattern-based review catches systematic issues in 10-15 minutes vs 40-60 minutes for full line-by-line.'
Reflection: 'AI adds auth (common pattern) but misses domain-specific ownership checks - this is why IDOR common in AI-generated code.'

learning_style_signals: prioritizes high-risk sections for deeper review
